heroBody: The Shen Foundation champions Asian diasporic artists as important makers in our time, cultivating a generative environment where bold ideas, experimental practices, and challenging projects can take form and circulate widely. It forges enduring relationships with artists grounded in trust, rigor, and curiosity, creating conditions in which new artistic languages, risks, and contradictions are supported and understood.

intro.title: What we do
intro.body: REWRITE We organize special temporary exhibitions and new commissions, working closely with artists to bring ambitious, large-scale projects into being. This work is built on trust, patience and long-term relationships — commissioning contemporary art takes time, and we're committed to doing it right.

people.name: Eleanor Shen
people.bio: Eleanor Shen is the founder of The Shen Foundation, a non-profit organization supporting contemporary artists of the Asian diaspora. She has served on the AGO Board of Trustees since 2015 and is currently a member of the People Committee and the Collections Committee. Internationally, she participates as a member of acquisition committees at Tate Modern and the Centre Pompidou, and as a member of the International Leadership Council at the New Museum. She also serves as a board member of the Hometowns Initiative. Previously, she has served on the boards of the Power Plant, the Canadian Art Foundation, Soulpepper Theatre Company, Partners in Art, and the Child Development Institute. She holds an MBA and spent her early career in finance.

people.name: Kitty Scott
people.bio: Kitty Scott is Director and Curator of the Shen Foundation. She is a leading curator, and writer whose work spans major art institutions and major international exhibitions. She is known for shaping contemporary art discourse through ambitious programming and sustained collaborations with artists. Scott has held key curatorial posts including Curator of Contemporary Art and later Deputy Director and Chief Curator at the National Gallery of Canada in Ottawa. She also served as the Carol and Morton Rapp Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art at the Art Gallery of Ontario in Toronto. Previously, she was Chief Curator at London’s Serpentine Gallery and Director of Visual Arts here at The Banff Centre, where she oversaw residencies, exhibitions and the Banff International Curatorial Institute. Scott was appointed Chief Curator of the 15th Shanghai Biennale, 2025-26 and was a core agent for dOCUMENTA (13) in 2012. With Sally Tallant she co-curated the 2018 Liverpool Biennial, “Beautiful world, where are you?”. In 2017 she curated Geoffrey Farmer’s exhibition for the Canada Pavilion at the 57th Venice Biennale. Across these roles she has championed a wide range of contemporary artists while publishing extensively in catalogues, books and journals.
